guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not dismissing Ohio State’s offensive start. The Buckeyes averaged 45.0 points and 522.0 yards through four games, while Jeremiah Smith had already produced 617 receiving yards and seven touchdowns. That passing-game ceiling is the clearest concern for our Indiana position, and it explains why the market is comfortable pricing Ohio State as the stronger side.

For us, the disagreement starts with Indiana’s ability to challenge Ohio State on the ground. Our numbers rate Indiana’s rush defense far better than Ohio State’s rushing offense, creating a path for the Hoosiers to make the Buckeyes more one-dimensional. We also see more uncertainty in Ohio State’s defense than the early results suggest: only three defensive starters returned after eight were lost from the 2025 unit. Ohio State allowed just 12.3 points per game through four games, but our longer-run view does not treat that small sample as definitive. That combination gives us enough reason to support Indiana at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Ohio State’s passing offense against Indiana’s pass defense. Julian Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes with 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions in 2025, and our metrics again place the Buckeyes’ passing attack among the nation’s best. Indiana does not need to erase that advantage, but our case becomes much stronger if its run defense forces Ohio State to rely heavily on the tougher, more variable part of the matchup.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned eight offensive starters: Julian Sayin, Bo Jackson, Jeremiah Smith, Brandon Inniss, Phillip Daniels, Carson Hinzman, Luke Montgomery and Austin Siereveld.
The Buckeyes lost starting tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek and starting guard Tegra Tshabola from the 2025 team.
Ohio State's starting offensive line had combined for 154 games played and 101 starts.
Ohio State had 85.8 percent offensive-line continuity based on returning snaps by players who logged at least 100 snaps in 2025, the highest percentage among Power Four teams.

Tight end Mason Williams transferred from Ohio with career totals of 51 receptions, 600 yards and six touchdowns.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned three defensive starters: cornerback Jermaine Mathews Jr., defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.
Ohio State lost eight defensive starters from 2025: Tywone Malone Jr., Kayden McDonald, Caden Curry, Arvell Reese, Sonny Styles, Caleb Downs, Lorenzo Styles and Devin Igbinosun.
Safety Earl Little Jr., a Florida State transfer, led Ohio State with 23 tackles through four games.
Linebacker Riley Pettijohn led Ohio State with four tackles for loss and two sacks through four games.
Defensive tackle James Smith and defensive end Qua Russaw transferred from Alabama.
Linebacker Christian Alliegro transferred from Wisconsin with career totals of 141 tackles and eight sacks.
Defensive tackle John Walker transferred from UCF with career totals of 72 tackles, eight tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's 2026 coordinators are defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, offensive coordinator Arthur Smith and special teams coordinator Robby Discher.
Tyler Bowen serves as run game coordinator and offensive line coach, while Billy Fessler is pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
